conclusions: All finite limits and finite colimits exist in $\mathcal{A}$.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an abelian category.
All finite limits and finite colimits exist in $\mathcal{A}$.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: There exists a covering refining both given coverings.
hypotheses: Two coverings of the same object $U$ in a site $\mathcal{C}$.
statement:
Given a pair of coverings $\{U_i \to U\}$
and $\{V_j \to U\}$ of a given object $U$ of the site
$\mathcal{C}$, there exists a covering which is a
common refinement.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: It extends uniquely to a groupoid $(U,R,s,t,c)$ over $S$.
hypotheses: An equivalence relation $j:R\to U\times_S U$ over $S$.
statement:
Given an equivalence relation $j : R \to U \times_S U$ over $S$
there is a unique way to extend it to a groupoid
$(U, R, s, t, c)$ over $S$.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: That direct summand has a left dual.
hypotheses: A Karoubian additive monoidal category; a direct summand of an object with a left dual.
statement:
In a Karoubian additive monoidal category every summand
of an object which has a left dual has a left dual.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: The morphism $j:R\to U\times_S U$ is a pre-equivalence relation.
statement:
Given a groupoid scheme $(U, R, s, t, c)$ over $S$
the morphism $j : R \to U \times_S U$ is a pre-equivalence
relation.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: The functor $C$ is exact and reflects injections and surjections.
statement:
For a ring $R$, the functor $C : \text{Mod}_R \to \text{Mod}_R$ is
exact and reflects injections and surjections.

conclusions: It is an abelian group scheme; its group law is commutative.
statement:
An abelian variety is an abelian group scheme, i.e., the group
law is commutative.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: The associated adjoint functors $(f^{-1}=u_s,f_*=u^s)$ form a morphism of topoi.
hypotheses: A morphism of sites $f:\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}$ corresponding to $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$.
statement:
Given a morphism of sites $f : \mathcal{D} \to \mathcal{C}$
corresponding to the functor $u : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{D}$
the pair of functors $(f^{-1} = u_s, f_* = u^s)$ is a morphism of topoi
$\Sh(\mathcal{D}) \to \Sh(\mathcal{C})$.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.

conclusions: It satisfies the stated universal generation and relations properties.
hypotheses: The simplex category $\Delta$ with objects $[n]$ and its face and degeneracy morphisms.
statement:
The category $\Delta$ is the universal category
with objects $[n]$, $n \geq 0$ and morphisms
$\delta^n_j$ and $\sigma^n_j$ such that (a) every morphism is
a composition of these morphisms, (b) the relations
listed in Lemma \ref{lemma-relations-face-degeneracy} are satisfied,
and (c) any relation among the morphisms is a consequence of
those relations.
statement_editorial_notes: Source-statement-only editorial split; no mathematical/proof verification.
